stories.title: A Few Thoughts about the Texans Game - In no particular order
stories.summary:
I honestly don't even know how to kick this one off as my mind is absolutely racing after this game.  I easily took more notes during this game than I ever had for any Bills game.  I came into the game prepared for a loss, not out of negativity but just out of the reality of playing a really tough Texans team on the road.  I was excited to see the benefits of the coaching change (even though there were plenty of moments where it felt like the same old McD Bills), how aggressive the Leonard 3-4 defense was (or not...) and what version of Josh I would see (God Mode Activated). With that, here's my best attempt to organize all of my thoughts.  Sorry for the last of lyrics @Bill from NYC.



	 



	1 - Josh - I know it's only one game, but Josh looked like Josh-Prime to me. The designed runs on the first drive surprised me a little considering the defense we were playing, but it became pretty clear that Brady wasn't going to put restrictions on him. The long touchdown run was vintage Josh and he made some ridiculous throws throughout the game. The Kincaid catch was obviously spectacular, but the throw was right there too. Same with the Palmer touchdown. After Palmer didn't even look for the ball on what could have been an interception the play before, Josh comes right back to him and throws an absolute strike for the touchdown. That's Josh. It wasn't perfect. The fumbled snap followed by the missed deep ball to Moore and tipped pass was an absolutely terrible series. He also had Shakir wide open in the end zone on the third down where his arm got hit. Overall, 30+ points, no offensive turnovers, and multiple touchdowns from Josh on the road against this defense should have been more than enough.



	 



	2 - New Defense, Same Third Downs? - This might be my biggest concern coming out of the game. I was excited all offseason about the idea that we could rush four and actually generate pressure without needing to blitz. On the Texans' first third and long, Groot and Oliver did exactly that and forced the Stroud fumble. Beautiful. That's exactly what I wanted to see.Then it disappeared for huge stretches of the game.How many 3rd and longs did we give up because Stroud had all day? Rush four, nothing. Rush five, nothing. Stroud even scrambled for a first on one of them. There were multiple plays where the receiver was just sitting wide open beyond the sticks. I understand that you're not going to get home every play, but you can't repeatedly put an offense in 3rd and long and then make it look easy. That's painfully familiar.The good news? When we absolutely had to have it, the pass rush finally showed up. Walker's sack on 1st and goal was massive and Groot ending the game with the strip sack was exactly the type of play we've been begging this defensive line to make for years. So maybe there's something here. But man, that was a frustrating way to get there.



	 



	3 - Groot - If you're going to get paid like one of the foundational pieces of this defense, this is what I want to see. Groot was around the ball all game. He and Oliver created the early turnover, he blew up a play action later, and then when the entire game came down to the defense getting one stop, Groot ended it himself with the strip sack.That's the type of impact game I've been waiting to consistently see from him. Not pressures. Not almost getting there. Game-changing plays. If this defense is going to work the way Leonard wants it to, Groot needs to be one of the guys who makes it work. Great start.



	 



	4 - Tackling - Holy crap was this bad early. Walker whiffed. Benford whiffed. Williams missed one and was getting eaten alive by blockers. Houston's first touchdown drive ended with three straight runs and there were way too many plays where the first Bills defender to the ball didn't finish the play.This is also where I have to remind myself that it's Week 1 in a completely new defense. There are going to be communication issues and guys figuring out responsibilities at full speed. But tackling isn't a scheme issue. That's basic football and it needs to get cleaned up immediately.



	 



	5 - Benford - This was probably one of the more surprising performances to me after watching Benford at the scrimmage and knowing what he's capable of. Collins gave him problems. He had the PI and then gave up the touchdown before halftime on a drive where Houston basically walked down the field against our prevent defense. I'm not worried about Benford after one game, especially against a receiver like Collins, but this definitely wasn't the shutdown performance we've become accustomed to seeing from him. I'm much more interested in seeing how he responds next week.  However, I do want to give Benford some grace as it's taken him a few games to get going in prior seasons, so I choose to believe he'll get there.



	 



	6 - Brady - There were things I liked. They clearly wanted to establish the run early. We got designed Josh runs immediately. The Okie Dokie worked again with Coleman finding Shakir. We took some shots downfield. There was finally a swing pass to Cook, even if it went nowhere. Overall, the offense scored 30+ points against a good Houston defense without turning the ball over. I'll take that every week. But there were still some Brady moments. Too many men in the huddle is on him. The back-to-back ineligible man downfield penalties were brutal. And what the hell was that two-point conversion? This continues to be an issue. We have Josh Allen and somehow our two-point plays consistently look like we drew them up in the huddle. I don't understand it. Still, if my biggest complaint about Brady after Week 1 is a failed two-point conversion when his offense scored 30+ without a turnover, I'm not going to go crazy yet.



	 



	7 - DJ Moore - Well, hello there. The PI on the deep ball was nice, but the touchdown was the moment. That's exactly what I hoped we were getting when we added him. Someone who can create an explosive play and give Josh another legitimate option beyond Shakir and Kincaid. The receivers weren't dominant overall, but Moore gave us something we desperately lacked at times last season. I want to see more shots to him because Josh clearly isn't afraid to throw it deep this year.  



	 



	8 - Special Teams - Hoecht apparently decided that if he wasn't going to get to Stroud, he was going to murder someone on kick coverage instead. He blew up the first return and made another great tackle later. Buffalo Joe also destroyed a return early. Whatever they're doing with the kickoff coverage, I enjoyed watching it. And shout out to Bass. Perfect day. No drama. No staring at the uprights wondering what fresh hell awaits us. Just make your kicks and let me forget you're there. Please and thank you.



	 



	9 - Cap Space - Anyone happen to have an extra 40 mil laying around?  Looks like we are going to need it after this season for Kincaid and then eventually Walker.  I mean, wow.  If these two guys can keep this going and stay healthy, look out.  Kincaid was an absolute beast in every way possible.  High point catches, run after catch, and overall mismatch dominance.  Walker also just dominated at the point of attack.  Watching him just throw grown men around, chase Stroud to the sideline, and drop guys behind the LOS was super impressive.  



	 



	10 - Leonard - I genuinely don't know how I feel about the defensive debut. There were moments where I saw exactly what got me excited all offseason. Four-man pressure creating a turnover. Groot making impact plays. Walker blowing up a screen and then getting the huge sack late. IGB making a big third-down breakup. The defense forcing a three-and-out when the offense desperately needed the ball back. And finally, when the game was completely on them, Groot ends it. There were also stretches that were terrible. Missed tackles everywhere. Williams getting swallowed by blockers. No pressure on multiple 3rd and longs. Collins abusing Benford. A prevent defense before halftime that prevented absolutely nothing. A completely blown coverage on Montgomery's touchdown. Twelve men on the field after a timeout. Hairston looking confused while Noel runs wide open on the biggest drive of the game. That's a lot. But this is also where I'm going to give Leonard the grace I talked about before the season. It's Week 1. It's an entirely new defense with new players being asked to do different things. I expected big plays in both directions and that's pretty much exactly what we got. Most importantly, when they absolutely needed a play to win the game, they made one.



	 



	*Bonus - Where were you? - Parker, Chubb, CJGJ and Coleman were basically non-existent to me. I'm sure I'll see things on the rewatch that I missed, and not everyone is going to fill up the stat sheet every week, but those are guys I expected to notice.



	 



	**Double Bonus - Refs - I don't like blaming officials and I'm not going to pretend everything went against Buffalo, but they were way too involved in this game. The defensive holding on Alford where the receiver basically ran into him was ridiculous. Then we get another ticky-tack defensive holding call later. Benford gets called. Back-to-back offensive holding penalties kill a drive. There were legitimate penalties in there too, but I don't watch football to see flags become one of the major storylines of the game. Let them play.



	 



	 



	What a fantastic win that I don't think anyone saw us winning in that fashion. Going into Houston and winning against a team that has given us problems is a great way to start the Brady era. Josh looked like Josh. The offense put up 30+ without turning the ball over. The defensive line created two massive turnovers and ended the game when it had to. Was it clean? Absolutely not. But maybe that's actually what I like about it. The Bills didn't need to play a perfect game to go into Houston and win. There is a ton to clean up, especially defensively, and we still walked out 1-0. I'll take that.



	 



	Go Bills!!!!

stories.title: POWER RANKINGS - Week 1
stories.summary:
ESPN: https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/49881711/power-rankings-week-2-all-teams-top-newcomers-debuts



	 



	1. Buffalo Bills (1-0)



	Week 1 result: Beat the Texans 36-31
	Preseason ranking: 3



	Non-QB newcomer debut: WR DJ Moore



	Moore's five catches for 100 yards were somewhat aided when Houston safety Reed Blankenship went for an interception and missed badly, giving Moore an easy path to a 43-yard touchdown. However, Moore also did a lot of things that didn't end up in his standard receiving totals. He drew a 46-yard pass interference penalty and later an illegal contact flag. He also slapped away what appeared to be a very likely interception for Houston safety Calen Bullock. It was everything the Bills could have asked for when they traded for Moore in March. -- Aaron Schatz



	 



	Yahoo: https://sports.yahoo.com/nfl/article/nfl-power-rankings-entering-week-2-what-do-we-make-of-the-rams-without-myles-garrett-040841481.html



	 



	1. Buffalo Bills (1-0, LW: 3)



	Had Bills-Texans happened in prime time, as it should have, we'd be even more excited about what Josh Allen did against a very good Houston defense. The 36 points the Bills put up was the most against Houston since 2023, which was DeMeco Ryans' first season as head coach. Allen threw for 334 yards and two touchdowns and rushed for 23 yards and two touchdowns. That win was a statement. The fact that it happened in the 1 p.m. Eastern window just means the Bills won't get as much hype as they should. That might change Thursday night when they face the Lions.



	 



	 



	NFL.com: https://www.nfl.com/news/nfl-power-rankings-week-2-2026-nfl-season



	 



	2. Buffalo Bills 1-0



	The Bills exorcised the horned demon that has haunted them in Houston, lighting up the Texans' fearsome defense to the tune of 36 points and 409 yards, including a 96-yard touchdown drive with the game on the line. Josh Allen kicked off his latest MVP push with a signature performance, throwing for 334 yards and two touchdowns while rushing for two more scores, delivering a trademark Buffalo win in Joe Brady's debut as head coach. Good start, Bills Mafia.



	 



	-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------



	 



	I guess folks think we're pretty good. Maybe not as bad as our fans think... 



	 


	 



	I know these dont mean much, but after suffering through 20 years of disrespect, it's still nice to see.



	 



	Praise Josh!

Buffalo Sabres Top 25 Under 25: #3 Josh Doan
stories.summary:
The Top 25 Under 25 is a collaboration by members of the Die By The Blade community. 92 readers ranked Buffalo Sabres players under the age of 25 as of August 1, 2026. Each participant used their own metric of current ability and production to rank each player.



Josh Doan



Drafted: 2021 Second Round, #37 overall



Size: 6’2″, 198 lbs



Position: Winger (shoots right)



Born: 2/1/2002 (Age: 24) Scottsdale, AZ



2025-2026 stats: GP82 G25 A27 PTS52, Buffalo Sabres (NHL)



2025 T25U25 Ranking: 8th



This is how we started last year’s T25U25 for Doan – 




It’s truly unfortunate that every movement Josh Doan makes is going to be examined under the microscope of the JJ Peterka trade. In case you forgot, the 23-year-old comes to Buffalo along with defenseman Michael Kesselring from Utah Mammoth with the young German forward going the other way. It definitely was a controversial trade that many will say the Sabres got fleeced in, while others maintain that as long as both sides get what they wanted out of it, it’s a fair hockey trade. Only time will tell.




A year later, Kesselring is a distant memory traded away to the Sharks for the Sabres to move up seven spots in the Draft and pick up Ilia Morozov. Meanwhile Doan has been an unqualified success, logging 52 points outscoring Peterka who had 47 points and was then flipped to the Boston Bruins for two first rounders, in 2026 and 2028. 



The Son of Doan has become an integral part of the Sabres top six, getting minutes on the right side of the powerplay unit as well. His 17 points with the man advantage was third behind only Rasmus Dahlin and Tage Thompson.









So where does Josh Doan go from here? 



Buffalo tried real hard to keep Alex Tuch, and reports indicate they were willing to pay him nearly $10 million a year too, but eventually the Syracuse-native decided he wanted to go to Washington instead. At some point the Sabres decided that Doan was an in-house, more than ready-made replacement for him, especially since the 24-year-old led Buffalo with 2.12 takeaways per 60, while Tuch was at 1.55. 



Doan is not afraid to be physical, throwing the body where needed with 3.59 hits/60, but it’s the timing of when he chooses to do so was what was incredible, especially in the Bruins series when it went up to 7.07 hits/60.









Doan signed a seven-year, $48.65 million contract extension in January 2026, which is actually just higher in AAV than the extension Noah Ostlund signed yesterday. For the $6.95 million AAV, the Sabres are certainly getting excellent value for what they have him locked up for, with comparables such as Troy Terry who matched his scoring output in just 51 games, Nazem Kadri who had 50 pts in 77 GP and Anders Lee who got to 42 pts in 82 GP.



He’s quickly become a fan favorite with his work ethic and Doan has shown that he is indeed his father’s son with his no prisoners taken playing style. The Sabres certainly got a gem of a hockey player in Josh Doan.

stories.title: Buffalo Sabres sign Noah Ostlund to long-term extension
stories.summary:
With training camp just around the corner, the Buffalo Sabres announced that young forward Noah Ostlund has inked an eight-year extension with an AAV of $6.6 million. This represents a handsome raise for the 22-year-old who has seen his role with the Sabres grow in the last couple of seasons, with Ostlund entering the last year of his current three-year deal an AAV of just $886,666. 



Ostlund played in eight games in Buffalo in the 2024-25 season but became indispensable with the Rochester Americans, going 45GP 19G 17A 36pts. However, last season he made the step up and scored 3G and 7A in ten games for the Amerks, but spent the majority of the time with the Sabres playing in 60 games, with 11G and 16A for 27 points in all. It was in the playoffs though that he made the biggest impression, and irreversibly turned the series against the Boston Bruins in the Sabres favor in just three games before he went out injured. Buffalo could have certainly used him in the tight series to come with the Montreal Canadiens when they were edged out in overtime of Game 7. 



The Swedish-born forward is expected to stay in Buffalo this season and compete for a spot in the top six, and extending him at a cost-controlled rate represents excellent value again for the Sabres who have built up a stable of young talent all at reasonable cap hits. 



It does appear that the Sabres’ comparable for the extension they handed Ostlund was Frank Nazar of the Chicago Blackhawks, who was given a 7-year extension last summer for $6.60M AAV, and he potted 15 goals and 26 assists for 41 points in 66 games last season. 



What is fascinating about this contract is that it’s more in the line of the “Dylan Cozens / Tage Thompson” style max-term roll of the dice—buying up almost entirely UFA years based on projection rather than the traditional 2-to-3-year bridge deals at a lower dollar amount. Clearly Ostlund also believes in whatever Jarmo Kekäläinen is selling because he is choosing to commit his long-term future to Buffalo.

stories.title: Buffalo Sabres Top 25 Under 25: #4 Konsta Helenius
stories.summary:
The Top 25 Under 25 is a collaboration by members of the Die By The Blade community. 92 readers ranked Buffalo Sabres players under the age of 25 as of August 1, 2026. Each participant used their own metric of current ability and production to rank each player.



Konsta Helenius



Drafted: 2024 – 1st Round (14th Overall)



Position: Center/Wing



Born: May 11th, 2006 – 20 Years Old



2025-2026 Stats: GP 63 G 21 A 42 PTS 63 / Playoffs GP 3 G 2 A 1 PTS 3, AHL



                             GP 9 G 1 A 3 PTS 4 / Playoffs GP 4 G 2 A 0 PTS 2, NHL



2025 T25U25 Ranking: 7



Konsta Helenius introduced himself to most Sabre fans this past season and made quite the impression. He spent most of the year in Rochester where he was the primary offensive play driver. Putting up 63 points in 63 AHL games is impressive for a 19-year-old. For comparison, JJ Peterka put up 68 points in 70 games for Rochester at the same age. He held his own during his 9-game regular season stint in Buffalo where he put up 4 points, including his first career NHL goal, in 9 games. The best part of his season came in the Spring.




KONSTA HELENIUS!!The @BuffaloSabres have a two-goal lead! 👏 #StanleyCup 🇺🇸: ABC🇨🇦: @Sportsnet & @TVASports pic.twitter.com/tSQT4wkZZl— NHL (@NHL) May 17, 2026




After Noah Ostlund went down in the Boston series, Buffalo needed an offensive spark against Montreal. That spark came in the form of Helenius. He made an immediate impact and helped round out the Sabres’ offensive lines. He finished with two goals in four playoff games, but he could have easily had two more. Before he finally got his first NHL playoff goal, he had two one-timer chances off nearly identical 2-on-1’s with Jason Zucker. One was victim of an incredible save, and the other crushed the post. He then went oversees to play for Finland in the World Championships. He looked great playing on Barkov’s wing. He put up 6 points in 6 games and joined Tage Thompson in an exclusive club by securing the gold medal with his overtime golden goal.




KONSTA HELENIUS GOLDEN GOAL IN OT‼️🇫🇮 #MensWorlds #IIHF pic.twitter.com/4HlCIFFZ8d— IIHF (@IIHFHockey) May 31, 2026




There are high hopes for Helenius this year as he will be counted on to replace some of the production Tuch had previously provided. He’s a offensive force with solid defensive instincts. One area of his game that goes largely unnoticed is his physical play. At 5’11”, he’s no imposing figure, put he finishes his checks, is relentless on the forecheck, and wins most of his board battles. Last year was Noah Ostlund’s coming out party, but this season could see Helenius go from a top prospect to a top contributor.

stories.title: Buffalo Sabres Top 25 Under 25: #5 Noah Ostlund
stories.summary:
The Top 25 Under 25 is a collaboration by members of the Die By The Blade community. 92 readers ranked Buffalo Sabres players under the age of 25 as of August 1, 2026. Each participant used their own metric of current ability and production to rank each player.



Noah Ostlund



Drafted: 2022, BUF (16th overall), 1st round, 16th pick



Position: Center, wing (shoots left)



Born: 3/11/2004 (Age: 22) Stockholm, SWE



2025-2026 stats: GP 60 G 11 A 16 PTS 27 +11, Buffalo Sabres



2025 T25U25 Ranking: 9th last year



Noah Ostlund put together a promising rookie year for the Buffalo Sabres during the 2025–26 NHL season, recording 11 goals and 27 points across 60 games. He missed time late in the year due to an upper-body injury starting around March 25, 2026, which sidelined him for several games before he returned for the playoffs. Noah was also temporarily sent down to the Rochester Americans in December not for performance, but as a procedural “numbers game” so the Sabres could carry an extra defenseman on a road trip since he didn’t require waivers. He would return soon after.



Ostlund earned praise from coach Lindy Ruff for his strong two-way play, responsible reads, and competitive board work despite a leaner physical frame. He also consistently drives play, creates high-danger chances, and makes his linemates better. All good things to hear about your first-year player. At 5’11” and 180, the staff would still like to see him fill out a bit more and add some muscle. That is one of the few complaints on Noah last season. The 22 year old sometimes looks like his Sabres’ sweater is two sizes too big.



Also a problem area is his faceoffs. Noah struggled on the dot with just a 31.9% faceoff win percentage, which restricted his usage as a full-time center.







The coaching staff loves what Ostlund can bring to the table, and so do the fans. He has a nose for the net and is highly creative offensively, with his playmaking ability standing out in particular. Ostlund possesses an excellent skill set and plenty of hockey smarts, all while handling his defensive responsibilities well. His physicality and durability should only improve as he adds more strength, allowing him to better withstand the full (and new) 84-game grind of the NHL.



This kid has a ton of potential, and the sky is truly the limit for him. If he can stay healthy and play close to a full season, he is capable of putting up 20 goals and 55 points this year. He was sorely missed after going down in the playoffs, managing a goal and an assist in his three games played. He should also see more power-play time this season, giving him another opportunity to boost his offensive numbers. To me, Noah Ostlund seems poised for a strong sophomore breakout when the puck drops this October. I don’t anticipate any second year jinxing to suddenly pop up with this fine player.

stories.title: Buffalo Sabres Top 25 Under 25: #6 Jiri Kulich
stories.summary:
The Top 25 Under 25 is a collaboration by members of the Die By The Blade community. 92 readers ranked Buffalo Sabres players under the age of 25 as of August 1, 2026. Each participant used their own metric of current ability and production to rank each player.



Jiri Kulich



Drafted: 2022 First Round, #28 overall



Size: 6’1″, 185 lbs



Position: Center (shoots left)



Born: 4/14/2004 (Age: 22) Kadan, CZE



2025-2026 stats: GP12 G3 A2 PTS5, Buffalo Sabres (NHL)



2025 T25U25 Ranking: 4th



After a breakout season when he came up to the big club from Rochester and made a spot on the top line his own, Jiri Kulich pretty much lost the whole of last season after being diagnosed with a serious blood clot. He underwent a successful procedure to have the blood clot surgically removed, and then resumed light, non-contact skating in May. During locker cleanout he confirmed he expects to resume his hockey career, and is expected to be a full participant in preseason training soon. 



It’s been so long since we’ve seen the Czech forward play that in many ways he’s going to be like a new signing for the team when he returns. Let’s not forget when he finished the 24-25 campaign, he was centering the top line and had earned Lindy Ruff’s trust in that key role. 









Kulich’s ace in the hole has been his shot, and arguably it’s the second-best one-timer on the team behind only Tage Thompson. That makes him a threat to opposing defenses who have been keying in on stopping Thompson, especially on the power play. With the man advantage and Kulich on ice, opponents will have to pick which poison they want to deal with. 



He has exceptional mobility in every direction, which not only allows him to beat defenders to the outside off the rush but he also uses that with an active stick to disrupt opponents backchecking. Kulich has been called ‘smart and sneaky‘. He is Zach Benson in many ways, but a much more rounded player than our carnie and that makes Kulich an intriguing prospect on his superstar track. 



The forward’s smooth skating and puck control even under pressure are other qualities that will strengthen the Sabres top six forward corps, and pose an even bigger threat. He has a career faceoff win percentage of 44.6% so that is one area he needs to work on, but should be in line for more minutes per night after averaging 15:03 in his first two seasons with Buffalo. 









Hopefully his blood clot issue is behind him and he can return to playing like he did two springs ago. The only reason Kulich dropped from #4 to #7 is because he missed a year – I will not be surprised at all to see him at #1 when we do this again next year.

stories.title: Buffalo Sabres Top 25 Under 25: #7: Jack Quinn
stories.summary:
The Top 25 Under 25 is a collaboration by members of the Die By The Blade community. 92 readers ranked Buffalo Sabres players under the age of 25 as of August 1, 2026. Each participant used their own metric of current ability and production to rank each player.



Jack Quinn



Drafted: 2020 – 1st Round (8th Overall)



Position: Winger



Born: September 19th, 2001 – 24 Years Old



2025-2026 Stats: GP 82 G 20 A 31 PTS 51 / Playoffs GP 13 G 2 A 5 PTS 7, NHL



2025 T25U25 Ranking: 6



Jack Quinn had the best season of his young career this past season. He set career highs in games played, goals, assists, and points while skating primarily with McCloud and Zucker on the third line. Lindy Ruff liked the chemistry between those three as he largely left the combination static throughout the season. It will be interesting to see if Ruff goes back to those three as a line for continuity purposes as they reshuffle their forward lines.




Insane play from Jack Quinn and Jason Zucker 🤩#LetsGoBuffalo pic.twitter.com/M4Ullk24NB— Buffalo Sabres (@BuffaloSabres) October 23, 2025




Quinn’s 51 points made him the 6th highest scoring player on the roster, but there is still room for him to grow. While he has become more consistent, there were stretches of last season where he’d seemingly disappear. He had three separate 4 game stretches with no points in the first half of the season. He was more consistent in the second half which helped Buffalo turn their season around in route to the division title. Buffalo needs the second half Quinn to resurface as they look to replace the departed production of Alex Tuch. Quinn will likely be asked to step into a larger role which gives him the opportunity to earn a significant payday at the end of the season. He will be a restricted free agent after next season.




JACK QUINN HAS TWO!! ✌️ #StanleyCup 🇺🇸: ABC🇨🇦: @Sportsnet & @TVASports pic.twitter.com/pnYsKFrBug— NHL (@NHL) May 17, 2026




One area Quinn showed significant improvement was his work along the walls. Particularly in the first half of the season, he was consistently losing battles which led to a lack of sustained offensive pressure. In the second half, he was much stronger in board battles and it significantly improved his effectiveness. Additionally, there were concerns about how effective he would be as the physicality of the game ramped up in the playoffs. After an unremarkable start against Boston, Quinn found his footing and was one of the more noticeable Sabre forwards against Montreal.



There is a lot to like about Quinn’s game. He will likely have the opportunity to go from a quality secondary scorer to become one of the Sabres primary scorers. Buffalo will need him to take another developmental step to build off last year’s success.

stories.title: Buffalo Sabres Top 25 Under 25: #8 Radim Mrtka
stories.summary:
The Top 25 Under 25 is a collaboration by members of the Die By The Blade community. 92 readers ranked Buffalo Sabres players under the age of 25 as of August 1, 2026. Each participant used their own metric of current ability and production to rank each player.



Radim Mrtka



Drafted: 2025, BUF (9th overall), 1st round, 9th pick



Position: Defense (shoots right)



Born: 6/9/2007 (Age: 19) Havlickuv Brod, CZE



2025-2026 stats: GP 43 G 1 A 33 PTS 34  Seattle Thunderbirds



2025 T25U25 Ranking: 13th last year



Here he is, folks. The highly talented but often-traded Radim Mrtka. And by “traded,” I mean by the fans, in countless fantasy deals designed to bring a big fish to Buffalo’s top-six. (or a certain goalie some want) With the Sabres’ glut of right-handed defensive prospects, Mrtka’s name has been thrown around more than any other. He may be a skilled young player, but in the eyes of some fans, he has also been deemed expendable.



That’s a little hard to square with the organization’s view of him. Buffalo selected Mrtka ninth overall in 2025, and the 6-foot-6 defenseman has already shown the combination of size, mobility, puck skills and defensive ability that made him such an intriguing pick. He put up 34 points in 43 WHL games last season and gained valuable experience with Rochester, playing 8 games at the end of the year.







Mrtka also finished as the highest-ranked defenseman prospect on this list, narrowly edging out newcomer Daxon Rudolph. (not counting established Owen Power) So what exactly is Radim? Is he one of Buffalo’s best trade assets, a tempting piece to dangle in pursuit of a big deal? Or is he the fine young defenseman they drafted, a player soon to be leading the rush up ice in Blue and Gold?



I think the answer may ultimately be either, if I am being honest. Buffalo sees Mrtka as a potential top-four defenseman, and with his rare combination of size, skating and two-way ability, it would be awfully premature to write him off as merely a trade chip. But there is no denying the value he has. Sabres’ GM Jarmo Kekäläinen seemingly offered him up at least once already (in the failed Colton Parayko trade) and may again for the right deal. There is also no denying the overabundance of right handed defenders working their way through Buffalo’s system.









Something has to give eventually. Whether Mrtka is the one who gets moved or Buffalo decides his talent is too valuable to part with, one or two of these right-handed defensemen are likely to find themselves on the move. For now, his combination of size, mobility and upside makes him a particularly fascinating piece of the puzzle.



Mrtka is expected to turn pro full-time in 2026-27, joining the Rochester Americans as he continues his development and works toward earning a future spot on the Sabres’ blue line. Buffalo’s player-development staff still views him as a potential top-four defenseman. Unless, of course, Jarmo says otherwise.

stories.title: Buffalo Sabres to appear on national TV 14 times during 2026-27 schedule
stories.summary:
Fresh off winning the Atlantic Division title, the Buffalo Sabres will be appearing on national television broadcasts 14 times during the upcoming season, NHL rights holders announced Wednesday.
The schedule features eight games on TNT/HBO Max, three games on ESPN or ABC’s channels and three exclusive games on ESPN+/Hulu (subscription streaming).

stories.title: Buffalo Sabres sell out of season tickets for 2026-27, create waiting list
stories.summary:
The Buffalo Sabres’ success last season created so much demand they’ve sold out of season tickets for the 2026-27 season, the team announced Tuesday.
So the Sabres, like they did in the mid-2000s, have started a season-ticket waiting list.

stories.title: Landon Jackson revisited.
stories.summary:
Everything I’ve read this summer about Landon Jackson says he is bigger, stronger, healthy, and looking like the player he was in college.  If true, this is great news for the Bills defense.  I was a fan of his in college and thought he could be an impact player for the Bills.  I was extremely disappointed last season that he looked awful before his season ending injury. 
	 



	Could he become a key piece of the new defense?  I saw a blurb on SI that Jackson could start ahead of TJ Sanders next to Oliver and Walker and he did start over Sanders in the 1st preseason game.  
	 



	Thoughts?

stories.title: NHL to produce games for Hurricanes, Blue Jackets, Wild, Blues
stories.summary: The Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes, along with the Columbus Blue Jackets, Minnesota Wild and St. Louis Blues, will have their games produced and distributed by the NHL for the coming season as the league branches out into centralized production.
